faqs.question: What should freelancers track?
faqs.answer: Track time by client and project, mark billable work consistently, and record notes that help explain the work. Use reports to check totals before billing.

faqs.question: How can I make time reports reliable?
faqs.answer: Record time close to when work happens, review entries regularly, and check project allocation, breaks, and rounding rules before invoicing.

faqs.question: Is automatic time tracking right for every freelancer?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Test how activity is captured, reviewed, corrected, and stored. Consider privacy and whether the resulting records are accurate enough for billing.

faqs.question: What costs should I include?
faqs.answer: Include seats, projects, reporting, invoicing, integrations, export, and the time required to correct entries and prepare client reports.

body:
Time Tracking Software for Freelancers: A Practical Buyer’s Guide

Freelancers may need to track billable hours, understand project effort, prepare client invoices, and keep records for their own bookkeeping. Choose a tool based on whether you need a simple timer, project reporting, invoicing, or a more automatic time-capture workflow.

Transparency note: Current prices, free-plan limits, and product claims have not been independently verified. Confirm current plan details and billing terms before relying on a free tier.

Tools to evaluate

Toggl Track

Test starting and stopping timers, correcting entries, assigning time to projects and clients, and exporting reports. Confirm current user limits and which billable reporting features are included.

Clockify

Test time entries, project and client organization, reports, and team access. Verify current free-plan limits for users, reporting, and administration.

Harvest

Evaluate the connection between time entries, project budgets, expenses, and invoicing. Test invoice export and payment workflow, and confirm which capabilities are included in the current plan.

FreshBooks

Evaluate time tracking alongside invoices, expenses, and bookkeeping. Test the path from a billable time entry to a client invoice, and confirm whether the accounting features fit your jurisdiction and workflow.

TrackingTime

Test timesheets, project assignment, team reports, and export. Confirm the current plan limits and whether the reporting format works for your clients.

Timely

Evaluate automatic or assisted time capture if you want to reduce manual entry. Test how suggestions are reviewed and corrected, what activity data is collected, and how privacy and access are controlled.

How to compare time trackers

  1. Track a representative week of client work and compare recorded time with your current process.
  2. Test edits, rounding rules, breaks, billable status, and project allocation.
  3. Generate a client-ready report and verify totals before using it for billing.
  4. Check integrations with calendars, project tools, accounting, and invoicing.
  5. Review privacy, data export, and how activity records can be corrected or deleted.
  6. Confirm current free-plan limits and total cost for your actual workflow.

Methodology

This is a practical buyer’s guide, not a verified price ranking. Use representative work, check reports before invoicing, and confirm current plan terms with vendors.
